chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about two chickens that were tied (by the legs), which I slaughtered while I was in Mecca in the state of Ihram. He said to me, 'Why did you slaughter them?' I said, 'A girl from the people of Mecca brought them to me and asked me to slaughter them, so I thought I was in Kufa and did not remember that I was in the Sanctuary (Haram), so I slaughtered them.' He said, 'Give their value in charity.' I said, 'And what is their value?' He said, 'A dirham is better than their value.'
And that which indicates that whenever he was in the state of Ihram, a blood (compensation) became obligatory upon him, added to what has preceded.

key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: One who is in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)
key_terms.مُسَرْوَلَيْنِ: Two animals with their legs tied together

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for mistakenly slaughtering game while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the compensation (*dam*) for a pilgrim who mistakenly slaughters game while in the state of *Ihram*, ruling that the value should be given in charity. The Imam’s specific instruction that 'a dirham is better than its value' highlights the principle of leniency and sufficiency in expiating such errors, distinguishing it from stricter penalties for intentional transgression. This establishes a foundational precedent in Shia jurisprudence for handling inadvertent violations of Hajr restrictions.
